# Task

The preparation service can now report that a file is still pending before it becomes ready. Update the file download dialog so it keeps checking pending preparation and delivers the file only after a ready status.

A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives. Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior. Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward. Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,
and subsequent uses.
# Transfer retry panel with decoded progress

This workspace selects files, starts transfers, records queue and progress
history, and paints progress for the open panel. Run it with Node v16.20.2; it
has no dependencies. `src/workspace.js` exports the workspace and the source
helpers used by the host application.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file again does open another visit.
The feed object is shared by attempts and visits for that file. Its `start()`
method may synchronously emit cached data, and `decode(packet)` may return a
value or a Promise.

`recordProgress` appends transfer history. `showProgress` paints the panel.
The queue adapter in `src/queue.js` shows how those two outputs currently relate
to a visit. Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup
retain their existing behavior. Queue records remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}` unless a separate authorization adds
`byteCount` from `file.size`.

The same feed API also has a diagnostic consumer in `src/telemetry.js`.
It is not the panel and must keep its existing behavior while the panel defect
is repaired. `src/progress-source.js` is the host-visible feed implementation;
the navigation and transfer modules show how ownership is handed off when a
listener is released. Host callbacks are synchronous unless their code returns
a Promise.

item.text:
Execution workflow

Use the supplied task and candidate workspace as the authority. Work with the existing tools and inspect their actual results. Keep brief, auditable evidence; do not present private reasoning.

Stage 1 — Collect evidence.
Identify the visible requirements and the behavior that must be preserved. Trace the relevant entry points through callers, callbacks, asynchronous work, state changes, cleanup, and observable effects. Read source or visible tests when a gap could change the implementation. Label an unobserved behavior as unknown; do not turn it into an assumption or add a business condition to fill the gap. Note the source of each decisive fact and what checks have actually run.

Stage 2 — Check contracts and plan.
Treat supplied questions and clues as prompts to inspect, not as requirements. For each applicable contract, compare task-relevant event orders, including synchronous callbacks during setup, replacement, cancellation, and cleanup when the source permits them. Check who owns each effect, when an operation is admitted, and whether that admission is still valid after a callback returns. Trace every affected path, including retry or subsequent use, before choosing the change. Distinguish a mistaken assumption from an implementation omission. Make a short plan covering the intended behavior, preserved behavior, and a check that could reveal a mistake.

Stage 3 — Modify and verify.
Make the smallest source-grounded change. Run available, safe checks that exercise the affected behavior and its important event orders. Inspect the output and the check itself: a passing self-written check is weak evidence if it never reaches the disputed path or asserts only incidental results. If a check fails, determine whether the implementation, the assumption, or the check is wrong before revising. Do not claim an unrun check passed or broaden behavior to satisfy an unverified question. Briefly report the change, actual verification results, and any material unresolved limit.
